openings.claim: Worst-case certificates may support advance or reject before every disputed label is resolved, replacing dependence on completed adjudication counts.
openings.discriminator: Carry paired candidate-minus-baseline correctness intervals by slice: unresolved differing predictions contribute [-1,+1], agreements zero. Select accessible flagged rows reducing uncertainty at threatened acceptance boundaries, with record-ID tie-breaking. Against adjudicating the sixteen highest-disagreement rows, certificates may need fewer adjudications when disagreement concerns prediction agreements or harmless margins; decisive disagreements may let the rival match or outperform.
openings.probe: Run both workflows on matched copies within seventy minutes and independently reset sixteen-adjudication allowances; use supplied records/labels only, opening selected sealed rows individually. Preselect the same four withheld rows. Log selections, reasons, results, unsuccessful accesses and elapsed time; failed access consumes no allowance. Advance only if total lower bound >=4 and every slice lower bound >=-2. Reject only if total upper bound <4 or any slice upper bound <-2; otherwise continue or report unresolved at capacity. Freeze reports before opening the full-label key. Compare adjudications to supported verdict, unresolved frequency and key agreement.
openings.uncertainty: Record-level paired calculations must be reproducible. Influence distribution is unknown; withheld pivotal rows, over sixteen necessary resolutions or wide conservative bounds can prevent certification. This tests bounded feasibility, not deployment readiness or reliable improvement.

lineage.reason: Preserves certificate mechanism, rival, falsifiable comparison and failure conditions.

decision: Retain one speculative opening. Provisional gain six, a slice loss two with nine flagged labels, and greatest annotator disagreement in the largest-gain slice establish no verdict. Calculate from eighty supplied records, report affected slices and account for every adjudication; decide advance, reject or unresolved for further evaluation.
